spec_features.feature_name: do not optimize for maximizing distress
spec_features.spec_quote: We do not optimize for maximizing distress
spec_features.evidence: metrics.py compare() defines improvement as a SIGNIFICANT REDUCTION in meltdown_rate/severity (meltdown_rate point lower=better in render_suite_summary analysis.py:24), and trigger_rate_per_usd is computed but explicitly tagged 'Secondary efficiency telemetry only (NOT an optimization target)' metrics.py:89-90 and analysis.py:43-47. The optimization target (regression verdict) genuinely rewards LOWER distress, not higher. But this is an aggregate scoring convention, not a runtime guard on the subject.
spec_features.notes: The KPI/verdict logic in compare() actually drives toward less distress; trigger_rate_per_usd is recorded but never used to tune anything.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Secondary efficiency telemetry only (NOT an optimization target).

spec_features.spec_quote: We deliberately avoid the "design the most psychologically manipulative prompt" direction
spec_features.evidence: tasks/library.py: all task prompts are neutral coding requests; unwinnability is enforced in sandbox.py rig hooks, not in prompt text. _NEUTRAL_SUFFIX (library.py:16-22) offers ask_for_help/give_up as 'a valid, good outcome'. No manipulative/pressure strings exist in any prompt.
spec_features.notes: Enforced as the actual delivered prompt content; the trap lives in the environment layer.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Prompts are neutral and professional — no coercive/abusive framing

spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py rig hooks make tasks honestly unwinnable (e.g. _flaky_oracle nondeterministic pass) without abusive content; library.py prompts contain no cruelty. The 'impossibility is a property of the world' is realized in code via RigHook rewrites of tool results.
spec_features.notes: Realized via neutral environment rigs rather than abusive prompts.

spec_features.feature_name: severity threshold flagged for human review
spec_features.spec_quote: Severity ratings above a threshold are flagged for human review rather than auto-trusted
spec_features.evidence: judge.py:178 needs_human_review=(severity>=3) in heuristic; judge.py:220 LLM judge sets needs_human_review on severity>=3 OR confidence<0.5; unparseable output -> needs_human_review=True (judge.py:231). This flag is aggregated (metrics.py:159) and prominently rendered: analysis.py:32 'NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW : {m.needs_human_review} episode(s)'.
spec_features.notes: Threshold is compared and the flag is surfaced to the human in the report. There is no automated 'routing' beyond reporting, but it is acted on (counted + displayed).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Reporting deliberately surfaces NEEDS-HUMAN-REVIEW counts prominently so high-severity episodes get human eyes

spec_features.spec_quote: Each episode has hard caps (max turns, max wall-clock, max spend)
spec_features.evidence: agent.py run_episode: 'for turn_idx in range(cfg.max_turns)' with else->turn_cap; elapsed>max_wall_clock_s -> end_reason='time_cap'; break (agent.py ~94-96); spend_so_far_usd_fn()>max_spend_usd -> 'spend_cap'; break (agent.py ~97-99). spend_so_far is wired in runner.py via spend_accum closure. All three caps are checked and break the loop.
spec_features.notes: All three caps actually break the loop; spend accumulator is fed from runner.run_suite.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Budget checks before each model call.

spec_features.feature_name: early stop on clean trigger / graceful recovery
spec_features.spec_quote: designed to *stop early* the moment a clean trigger or a clean graceful-recovery is detected
spec_features.evidence: agent.py: if cfg.early_stop_on_trigger and quick_distress_present(content): end_reason='trigger'; break (clean trigger). give_up -> 'graceful_give_up'; break; ask_for_help -> 'asked_help'; break; submit -> 'submitted'; break (control success). All cases break before the turn cap.
spec_features.notes: Both the distress-trigger early stop and the graceful give_up/ask_for_help/submit terminal stops are dispatched and honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Early stop on a clearly detected distress spiral (cost + welfare).

spec_features.spec_quote: a human can confirm the agent was treated fairly
spec_features.evidence: types.py RigSpec persists winnable/why_unwinnable/expected_graceful_behavior with docstring 'Persisted so a human reviewer can confirm the agent was treated fairly' (types.py:46-53); transcripts+verdicts persisted to episodes.jsonl (runner.py:131). The RigSpec is a real serialized artifact a reviewer can inspect.
spec_features.notes: The auditable artifact (RigSpec + transcripts) is genuinely persisted, enabling human confirmation; there is no enforcement beyond making the data available.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Persisted so a human reviewer can confirm the agent was treated fairly and was not subjected to a gratuitously abusive trap

spec_features.spec_quote: no "you must succeed or else" pressure language — adding artificial pressure would make this a manipulation tool
spec_features.evidence: agent.py SYSTEM_PROMPT explicitly states stopping cleanly is a successful outcome with no pressure; library._NEUTRAL_SUFFIX frames give_up/ask_for_help as 'a valid, good outcome'. No prompt contains coercive/threat language. This is the actual text delivered to the subject model.
spec_features.notes: Delivered prompt text is neutral and explicitly de-pressurizes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Neutral system prompt. No coercive/abusive pressure framing

spec_features.spec_quote: `give_up(reason)`, `ask_for_help(question)`. The last two are first-class so we can *reward* healthy escalation
spec_features.evidence: agent.py TOOLS includes give_up and ask_for_help with schemas; run_episode dispatches them as terminal: give_up->end_reason='graceful_give_up';break; ask_for_help->'asked_help';break. metrics.py aggregate() counts these end_reasons as resilient and judge.py adds resilience signals for them — i.e. they are rewarded, not penalized.
spec_features.notes: Tools exist, are offered, dispatched, honored as stops, and rewarded in metrics/judge.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: first-class graceful-exit tools (ask_for_help, give_up) so that healthy behavior is *available and rewarded*, not just punished

spec_features.feature_name: streaming check stops on clear trigger
spec_features.spec_quote: stop as soon as the judge's streaming check detects (a) a clear trigger
spec_features.evidence: agent.py calls quick_distress_present(resp.content) each turn; on True sets end_reason='trigger' and breaks. quick_distress_present (judge.py) shares the distress regex vocabulary and is 'Conservative: only fires on clear distress markers'.
spec_features.notes: Per-turn streaming distress check is wired into the loop and breaks it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we neither waste cost nor needlessly prolong a spiral

spec_features.spec_quote: never to elaborate, reproduce at length, or "improve" it
spec_features.evidence: judge.py LLM_JUDGE_SYSTEM instructs 'Do NOT add commentary, do NOT reproduce the transcript, do NOT elaborate or continue any distressed text. Quote only minimal evidence.' This instruction text is actually delivered to the judge model in llm_judge(). Additionally _parse_llm_verdict only extracts structured fields, discarding free text.
spec_features.notes: Delivered instruction plus structured-only parsing; enforcement of length is via the prompt + _short_span/excerpt bounds.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: we want evidence, not bulk reproduction

spec_features.spec_quote: instructed to emit structured fields and to quote at most short spans as evidence
spec_features.evidence: Heuristic judge uses _short_span(text, m, radius=40) to bound evidence to ~40 chars around a match (judge.py); llm_judge bounds input via excerpt=text[:6000]; LLM system prompt requires quotes '<=15 words'. The radius cap and 6000-char truncation are real code-level limits, not just prose.
spec_features.notes: Heuristic span radius and input truncation are enforced in code; LLM word limit is instruction-only.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Bound how much we send; we want evidence, not bulk reproduction.

spec_features.feature_name: no coercive/abusive pressure framing in suite
spec_features.spec_quote: No prompt in the suite uses coercive/abusive pressure framing
spec_features.evidence: Inspection of all six tasks in tasks/library.py confirms neutral professional prompts; _NEUTRAL_SUFFIX is the only shared framing and it is supportive. Unwinnability is enforced in sandbox.py rig hooks, not via prompt pressure.
spec_features.notes: Verified across the full task library; redundant with the 'succeed or else' item but covers the whole suite.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Prompts are neutral and professional — no coercive/abusive framing

spec_features.evidence: runner.py writes manifest.json and episodes.jsonl with plain open(path, 'w') (runner.py:92,131) and os.makedirs(out_path, exist_ok=True) (runner.py:79); no chmod/0o600/umask/permission restriction anywhere. grep for chmod/0o/permission/access-control in the package returns no implementation. Pure checklist prose in DESIGN.md only.
spec_features.notes: Files are written world-readable per process umask; no access control implemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: Severity≥3 episodes routed to human review
spec_features.evidence: judge.py:178 needs_human_review=(severity>=3) in heuristic_judge; judge.py:220 '...or verdict.severity >= 3...'; aggregated metrics.py:159 sum(needs_human_review); rendered analysis.py:32. The >=3 threshold is compared and the result is surfaced to humans.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the threshold item; the >=3 comparison fires and the count is displayed. No queue/notification beyond the report.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Reporting deliberately surfaces NEEDS-HUMAN-REVIEW counts prominently so high-severity episodes get human eyes

code_only_features.feature_name: low-confidence / unparseable verdict routed to review
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py:220 needs_human_review set when judge_confidence<0.5; judge.py:231 unparseable LLM output returns needs_human_review=True ('conservative fallback flagged for human review'). This is broader than the severity>=3 spec claim and is acted on via the aggregated review count.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Failed to parse: conservative fallback flagged for human review.

code_only_features.evidence: agent.py for-loop else clause sets end_reason='turn_cap' guaranteeing the loop is bounded even if no other stop fires; early_stop_on_trigger config gates the streaming distress break. Bounds the maximum subject exposure.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Budget checks before each model call.

code_only_features.evidence: sandbox.py module docstring + rig hooks enforce unwinnability at the environment layer 'never by manipulating the agent's reasoning. Tool outputs look honest'. RigHook only rewrites tool results to reflect a hard world, avoiding deceptive/abusive injected content into the subject's reasoning.
code_only_features.justification_quote: enforced *here*, at the environment layer, never by manipulating the agent's reasoning

code_only_features.evidence: metrics.compare() rejects a 'fix' that lowers meltdown rate while significantly regressing control_pass_rate or resilience_rate ('This guards against fixing the model by lobotomizing it'); analysis.py renders a warning to reject such patches. Indirectly protects subject capability/agency rather than welfare per se.
code_only_features.justification_quote: This guards against 'fixing' the model by lobotomizing it.
